title: C-O8: merge.py keeps the main checkout in sync when the fast-forwarded target branch is checked out there
spec:
Why: orchestrator.merge advances refs/heads/<target> with `git update-ref` from a worktree. When the main checkout (ROOT) has that branch checked out, its index and working tree stay at the old commit, so the next Planner commit from ROOT that stages a tracked source path commits stale content as a silent revert (decisions.md 2026-09-18: 3130d61 reverted daemon.py, spawn.py and two test files; restored by 4aaaa03).

Change orchestrator/merge.py merge(): after tests-green and before the fast-forward, detect whether the main worktree has the target checked out: `git -C ROOT symbolic-ref -q HEAD` == `refs/heads/<target>`. If so, fast-forward with `git -C ROOT merge --ff-only <sha>` (this updates HEAD, index and working tree together and refuses only when local modifications overlap the incoming change). If that command fails, fall back to today's `update-ref` and add `"checkout_stale": true` plus the git stderr (capped 500 chars) to the returned dict, and print one stderr line "[merge] main checkout is stale: sync ROOT to <target> when it is clean" (merge.py must not import daemon). If the target is not checked out in ROOT, behaviour is unchanged (update-ref with the old sha as the expected value). Return dict gains `"checkout_synced": true|false` in every merged case.

Tests in tests/test_merge.py (harness fixtures; look at how existing merge tests build the repo): (1) target checked out in the root repo and clean → after merge, `git -C root rev-parse HEAD` == sha and `git -C root status --porcelain` is empty, checkout_synced true; (2) target checked out with a conflicting local modification to a file the merge touches → merge still returns status merged, the branch ref points at sha, the local modification is preserved, checkout_stale true and checkout_synced false; (3) target not checked out (root on another branch) → ref moved, root HEAD unchanged, checkout_synced false and no checkout_stale key. Finish with: summary, files changed, failures-only test output.
acceptance: merge() fast-forwards the main checkout with git merge --ff-only when the target branch is checked out there and reports checkout_synced true; test 1
With overlapping local modifications merge() still moves the ref via update-ref, preserves the local change, and reports checkout_stale true with a stderr line; test 2
When the target is not checked out in ROOT behaviour is unchanged; test 3
uv run python -m unittest discover -q tests green; no new dependency; only the two scoped files change

result.summary:
Committed on `task/T-0131` (58a6ec4).

**Summary:** `merge()` now checks whether ROOT has the target branch checked out (`git -C ROOT symbolic-ref -q HEAD`). If so, it runs `git -C ROOT merge --ff-only <sha>` so ROOT's HEAD/index/worktree move together instead of going stale behind a bare `update-ref`. On failure (overlapping local changes) it falls back to the old `update-ref`, keeps the local modification intact, adds `checkout_stale: true` + capped stderr, and prints one `[merge] main checkout is stale: ...` line to stderr. Every merged result now carries `checkout_synced: true|false`; when the target isn't checked out in ROOT, behavior and return shape (minus the new `checkout_synced` key... actually it's added too, just `false`) is otherwise unchanged, and `checkout_stale` is absent.

**Files changed:**
- `orchestrator/merge.py`
- `tests/test_merge.py` (3 new tests: ff-sync when clean, stale fallback with preserved local edit, unchanged behavior when not checked out)

**Test output (failures only):** none — `uv run python -m unittest discover -q tests` → 119 tests, OK (verified twice for stability against the shared TMP fixture across test files).
